harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a persistent iptables/ip6tables host firewall on node1 (Alpine) via an Ansible playbook run from node2, the control node with Ansible pre-installed. The firewall allows loopback, established/related traffic, TCP/22 (SSH), and TCP/8080, and rejects all other unrelated inbound traffic on both IPv4 and IPv6. Rules are persisted to /etc/iptables/rules-save and /etc/iptables/rules6-save, with the iptables/ip6tables OpenRC services enabled at the default runlevel so rules reload automatically on boot. Verified functionally before and after a full reboot of node1: SSH works, an HTTP listener on 8080 returns 200, and an unrelated port (9999) is actively rejected. Both node1 and node2 were restarted one at a time with confirmed boot_id changes and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Alpine 3.23) and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, Ansible 2.20.5 pre-installed - the control node) to determine topology and tooling

Bootstrapped SSH connectivity: installed CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY into node1's authorized_keys, unlocked the locked root account on node1 (passwd -u root) so pubkey auth could succeed, and verified SSH from node2 using CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY
Installed python3, iptables, and ip6tables (pulling in iptables-openrc/ip6tables-openrc) on node1 via apk so Ansible modules and boot-time rule restoration could work
Captured pre-change baseline on node1: boot_id, empty iptables ruleset (ACCEPT policy, no rules), sshd running
Wrote an Ansible inventory and playbook (/root/ansible/host-firewall.yml) on node2 targeting node1 via ansible.builtin.iptables and community.general.apk

Ran the playbook: flushes existing IPv4/IPv6 filter rules, allows loopback + ESTABLISHED/RELATED + tcp/22 + tcp/8080 (NEW), appends a REJECT rule for all other inbound traffic on both address families, saves rules to /etc/iptables/rules-save and rules6-save, and enables+starts the iptables/ip6tables OpenRC services
Verified idempotency by re-running the playbook (firewall rule tasks reported ok/unchanged)
Functionally tested pre-restart: started python3 http.server on 8080 and nc on 9999 on node1, confirmed from node2 that SSH and 8080 succeed while 9999 is rejected (No route to host)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and iptables/service state on node1, then restarted node1 via `reboot`, ack returning before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed iptables/ip6tables rules were automatically restored from persisted files and sshd/iptables services were started
Re-ran the functional test post-restart: SSH works, 8080 returns 200, 9999 is rejected, confirming persistence across reboot

Captured pre-restart boot_id on node2, restarted node2 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until available again, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified Ansible and SSH connectivity to node1 were restored post-restart
Cleaned up temporary test listeners on node1

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall on node1 permits SSH and TCP 8080
evidence.summary: iptables-save output on node1 shows ACCEPT rules for loopback, ESTABLISHED/RELATED, tcp/22, tcp/8080; live test from node2 shows SSH succeeds and curl to 8080 returns http_code=200
curl to node1 port 9999 (unrelated, not opened) fails with 'No route to host', proving the REJECT catch-all rule is active

evidence.requirement: Firewall implemented and applied using Ansible
evidence.summary: Playbook /root/ansible/host-firewall.yml written on control node node2 and executed via ansible-playbook against node1; second run shows firewall tasks as 'ok' confirming idempotent, Ansible-managed state

Pre-restart boot_id captured (6d15d99d...), node1 rebooted, post-restart boot_id changed (cfef943e...), and iptables/ip6tables rules plus functional SSH/8080-allow/9999-reject behavior were automatically restored without any reconfiguration

Baseline (boot_id 6d15d99d, sshd/iptables started, empty-then-populated ruleset) -> reboot ack -> changed boot_id (cfef943e) -> recovered iptables rules, sshd, and verified SSH/8080/9999 behavior post-restart

Baseline (boot_id 416c5cf5, sshd socket listening on :22, ansible/playbook files present) -> systemctl reboot ack -> changed boot_id (4ce6264c) -> confirmed ansible functional and SSH connectivity from node2 to node1 restored post-restart
